content_preview.title: Android Studio Rabbit 2 Makes Bring Your Own Agent Stable and Android CLI Adds Device Streaming at Android Dev Summit; Quick Share SDK Due in 2027
content_preview.summary: Google's Android Dev Summit posts say Android Studio Rabbit 2 is stable with Bring Your Own Agent and Android CLI gains remote device and Compose preview commands; 9to5Google reports a Quick Share SDK for 2027.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Google marked Android Dev Summit on October 28 with a set of developer-tooling releases built around coding agents. According to the [Android Developers Blog](https://developer.android.com/blog/posts/ai-agents-android-studio-integration), Android Studio Rabbit 2 is now stable, and its Bring Your Own Agent (BYOA) feature lets developers choose agents including Claude Agent, Codex from OpenAI, Junie and Google Antigravity inside the IDE. The same day, Google's [summit roundup](https:/...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article (822 words, within the 400-1200 range) with Overview, What Shipped, Android CLI additions, Platform/Jetpack announcements, Quick Share SDK and Connected Apps, and a What We Don't Know section. Stable versus Canary/alpha/beta/preview stages are labelled consistently throughout.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 5 gzipped snapshots (source-0..4.html.gz, all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all) as extracted text. source-0 (developer.android.com, Matthew Warner, 28 Oct 2026): confirms 'Android Studio Rabbit 2 is now stable and ready for you to use in production' (verbatim), feature list (Bring Your Own Agent, new XR Emulator features, a LeakCanary update, a new agent skills manager tool, AI code review), 'over 40 coding agents - including Claude Agent, Codex from OpenAI, Junie, and Google Antigravity'. source-1 (developer.android.com roundup, Adarsh Fernando, 28 Oct 2026): confirms 'over 40 ACP-compatible coding agents', 'BYOA is now stable in today's release of Android Studio Rabbit 2', access to project structure and build, symbol resolution, Compose Preview rendering, Emulator, Logcat; Change Review (session from pending agent changes or Git changes window, report of potential issues, /review command); Migration Assistant 'available in the latest version of Android Studio Canary' (verbatim; correctly flagged as not in stable); android device remote (real physical device from a secure Google device lab, install/test like a local adb device); android preview (no emulator or IDE; 'In our internal testing, agents that used android preview completed UI tasks 77% faster while using up to 3x fewer tokens' - article labels this as Google's figure and notes no methodology); android analyze (R8 shrink/optimize/obfuscate, JSON for CI); Android CLI official agent plugin for Claude and Codex plus updated Antigravity plugin; Lightbuild early preview, strict YAML schema, 'while continuing to use Gradle and AGP for production apps' (verbatim); Android CLI launched 'earlier this year'; 'Fix with AI for memory leaks is available in the Android Studio canary build, and the memory leak subcommand is coming soon to Android CLI' (supports the What We Don't Know bullet). source-2 (developer.android.com, Matthew McCullough, 28 Oct 2026): confirms Rabbit 2 stable, Navigation 3 1.2 stable with deep links and richer Predictive back handling, AppFunctions 'Android's unified tool calling layer' now in beta, A2UI for Jetpack Compose in alpha, ML Kit Agentic API on Gemini Nano 4 in alpha, upcoming Compose 1.13 stable with Grid and Flexbox moving to stable, Core Jetpack XR SDK libraries stable, Connected Apps Platform preview. source-3 (9to5Google, Abner Li, Nov 2 2026): confirms Quick Share SDK 'coming in the first half of 2027', direct in-app integration instead of the system Share sheet, E2E encryption, automatic hotspot creation, Wi-Fi Direct on supported devices, offline operation, and a Quick Share iOS SDK; article attributes the timeline to 9to5Google. source-4 (9to5Google, Abner Li, Oct 28 2026): confirms Connected Apps Platform, cloud-hosted MCP server or Android MCP using AppFunctions APIs, Google Connected Console, preview signup with access opening 'in phases over the coming months'. Internal link /article/2026-05/20-android-studio-io-edition-... exists and the article does cover Android CLI (stable release, Claude/Codex mentioned), so 'also described Android CLI' is accurate. Independent-source count: 1 independent outlet (9to5Google, 2 articles, one of which is the only report of the Quick Share SDK); 3 sources are Google first-party. Not an Analysis, so no independence minimum applies.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All checked claims (versions, stable/beta/alpha stages, dates of Oct 28 and Nov 2, the 77% and 3x figures, 40+ agents, first half of 2027 for the Quick Share SDK, five quoted strings) trace to the snapshots. Quoted strings 'now stable and ready for you to use in production', 'available in the latest version of Android Studio Canary', 'while continuing to use Gradle and AGP for production apps', 'coming soon' and 'upcoming' are verbatim. Anthropic/OpenAI products are mentioned only attributively as agents/plugins per Google. The title claim 'Quick Share SDK Due in 2027' is supported by 9to5Google and attributed in the summary and body. Note: the Google roundup is internally inconsistent about LeakCanary in Android CLI (it first says 'now integrated directly into Android CLI with a new subcommand: android profiler leakcanary', then says the memory leak subcommand is 'coming soon'); the article reports the 'coming soon' line, which is a defensible reading and is described as unsettled in What We Don't Know.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; vendor claims are attributed ('Google says', 'Google describes') and the internal-testing figures are explicitly labelled as Google's with no published methodology. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers Android Dev Summit 2026, Rabbit 2, or the Quick Share SDK. The May 2026 Android Studio I/O Edition article is a different release and is linked as prior coverage.
concerns: Title is 146 characters (under the 150 limit but long and carrying two semicolon-joined stories).
Quick Share SDK is single-sourced to 9to5Google (no Google first-party post among the cited sources); the article attributes it correctly.
Three of five sources are Google first-party posts, so the independent-source base is thin (one outlet), appropriate for a News article but worth noting.
Google's own roundup contradicts itself on whether the LeakCanary CLI subcommand has shipped; the article follows the 'coming soon' statement.
recommendations: Prefer a shorter title for multi-topic roundups.
Where possible, add an independent outlet or a first-party Google post for secondary announcements such as the Quick Share SDK.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed News coverage of Google's Android Dev Summit developer-tooling announcements, with stable versus preview stages carefully separated and vendor performance figures labelled as Google's. Ready for publication without corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid release coverage for Android developers and agent-tool users, but largely incremental vendor announcements rather than an industry-changing story
